Shared Parameter Models

The defining feature of the Wu–Carroll (1988) shared parameter model is that the random effects of the focal model appear as predictors in the missingness model. Because the same latent variables drive both the outcome and nonresponse, they induce an association between Y and M. Any random effect in the focal model can play this role, which makes the model readily applicable to intensive repeated measures data. All models continue to use dummy-coded time. Results for every model are collected in the Sensitivity Analysis Results section.

Growth Data With Dropout

With attrition, the first occasion is structurally complete. The SEM omits the first dropout indicator; the MLM instead needs a time-varying dummy variable D (0 at baseline, 1 afterward) whose products with the random effects switch their influence on at occasions where dropout can occur.

\[M^*_{ti} = \lambda_0 + \sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\left[\lambda_{t0}(O_{ti}) + \lambda_{t1}(O_{ti})(\mathit{GROUP}_i)\right] + \lambda_1(\alpha_i)(D_{ti}) + \lambda_2(\beta_i)(D_{ti}) + z_{ti}\]

The \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\) terms induce the MNAR mechanism. The fixed intercept of –3 plays the role of omitting the baseline indicator, the occasion dummy codes allow occasion-specific dropout rates, and the interactions with D confine the random effects to post-baseline occasions, so the model is fully equivalent to the latent curve shared parameter model.

Model 2: Random Effects Predicting Attrition

The missingness block adds the switched random effects to the dummy-coded dropout model from the previous section.

Important features of the specification:

  • d = ifelse(time < 1, 0, 1); defines the switch (0 at baseline, 1 afterward).
  • alpha*d beta*d are the random intercept and slope, activated after baseline.
  • The level2: labels @g0a, @g1a, @g0b, @g1b are used by PARAMETERS and, in Model 4, by the residual definition variables.

Blimp script

DATA: growth-dropout.csv;                                # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                             # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                         # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                            # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (monotone);                               # dropout indicator (monotone)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta;                               # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                       # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                       # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                        # random slope equation
  alpha ~~ beta;                                         # random effect covariance
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;                         # level-1 (focal) model
  missingness:
  d = ifelse(time < 1, 0, 1);                            # definition variable: switch dummy code
  m ~ intercept@-3 alpha*d beta*d | intercept@0;         # missingness model
  { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                              # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                             # random number seed
BURN: 25000;                                             # warm-up iterations
ITER: 25000;                                             # analysis iterations

rblimp

model2_gd <- rblimp(
  data = growth_dropout,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (monotone)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta',
  fixed = 'group time',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    alpha ~~ beta;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;
    missingness:
    d = ifelse(time < 1, 0, 1);
    m ~ intercept@-3 alpha*d beta*d | intercept@0;
    { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 25000,
  iter = 25000)

Model 3: Random Effects and Their Squares Predicting Attrition

A linear specification lets only one tail of the random effect distribution predict higher nonresponse. Adding squared random effects allows attrition to depend on both tails (for example, both rapid improvers and non-responders disengaging). Nonlinear effects of latent variables are computationally demanding and may require larger samples.

Important features of the specification:

  • alpha*d^2 and beta*d^2 are the squared random effects; because d is 0 or 1, d^2 = d, and the terms are the squares of alpha and beta activated after baseline.

Blimp script

DATA: growth-dropout.csv;                                            # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                                         # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                                     # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                                        # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (monotone);                                           # dropout indicator (monotone)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta;                                           # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                                   # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                                   # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                                    # random slope equation
  alpha ~~ beta;                                                     # random effect covariance
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;                                     # level-1 (focal) model
  missingness:
  d = ifelse(time < 1, 0, 1);                                        # definition variable: switch dummy code
  m ~ intercept@-3 alpha*d alpha*d^2 beta*d beta*d^2 | intercept@0;  # missingness model
  { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;              # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                                          # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                                         # random number seed
BURN: 25000;                                                         # warm-up iterations
ITER: 25000;                                                         # analysis iterations

rblimp

model3_gd <- rblimp(
  data = growth_dropout,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (monotone)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta',
  fixed = 'group time',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    alpha ~~ beta;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;
    missingness:
    d = ifelse(time < 1, 0, 1);
    m ~ intercept@-3 alpha*d alpha*d^2 beta*d beta*d^2 | intercept@0;
    { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 25000,
  iter = 25000)

output(model3_gd)

Model 4: Random Effect Residuals Predicting Attrition

When the focal model includes predictors of the random effects, as it does here, alpha and beta in the missingness model are composites that include the group effect, so \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\) are not pure estimates of MNAR signal. The alternative uses the level-2 residuals, isolating the component of each random effect that is orthogonal to its predictors. The residuals are computed at every MCMC iteration from the current random effects and the current level-2 coefficients.

\[\zeta_{\alpha i} = \alpha_i - \left[\gamma_{0\alpha} + \gamma_{1\alpha}(\mathit{GROUP}_i)\right] \qquad \zeta_{\beta i} = \beta_i - \left[\gamma_{0\beta} + \gamma_{1\beta}(\mathit{GROUP}_i)\right]\]

Important features of the specification:

  • alpha_res = alpha - (g0a + g1a*group); and beta_res = ... are definition variables that subtract the level-2 predicted values; the labels g0a, g1a, g0b, g1b refer to the coefficients named in the level2: block.
  • This model needed 100,000 iterations to reach adequate diagnostics.

Blimp script

DATA: growth-dropout.csv;                                 # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                              # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                          # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                             # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (monotone);                                # dropout indicator (monotone)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta;                                # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                        # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                        # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                         # random slope equation
  alpha ~~ beta;                                          # random effect covariance
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;                          # level-1 (focal) model
  missingness:
  alpha_res = alpha - (g0a + g1a*group);                  # definition variable: intercept residual
  beta_res = beta - (g0b + g1b*group);                    # definition variable: slope residual
  d = ifelse(time < 1, 0, 1);                             # definition variable: switch dummy code
  m ~ intercept@-3 alpha_res*d beta_res*d | intercept@0;  # missingness model
  { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;   # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                               # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                              # random number seed
BURN: 100000;                                             # warm-up iterations
ITER: 100000;                                             # analysis iterations

rblimp

model4_gd <- rblimp(
  data = growth_dropout,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (monotone)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta',
  fixed = 'group time',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    alpha ~~ beta;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;
    missingness:
    alpha_res = alpha - (g0a + g1a*group);
    beta_res = beta - (g0b + g1b*group);
    d = ifelse(time < 1, 0, 1);
    m ~ intercept@-3 alpha_res*d beta_res*d | intercept@0;
    { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 100000,
  iter = 100000)

output(model4_gd)

Growth Data With Intermittent Missingness

With missingness at every occasion, the random effects can influence nonresponse over the whole study, so no switch is needed. The fixed intercept is estimable, the group main effect returns, and a random intercept allows person-level missingness propensities to vary.

\[M^*_{ti} = \lambda_0 + \lambda_1(\mathit{GROUP}_i) + \sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\left[\lambda_{t0}(O_{ti}) + \lambda_{t1}(O_{ti})(\mathit{GROUP}_i)\right] + \lambda_2(\alpha_i) + \lambda_3(\beta_i) + u_i + z_{ti}\]

Model 2: Random Effects Predicting Missingness

The missingness block adds alpha and beta to the dummy-coded intermittent model.

Important features of the specification:

  • m ~ intercept group alpha beta | intercept; – all parameters are free, including the random intercept after the pipe.

Blimp script

DATA: growth-intermittent.csv;                           # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                             # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                         # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                            # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (missing);                                # missingness indicator (intermittent)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta;                               # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                       # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                       # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                        # random slope equation
  alpha ~~ beta;                                         # random effect covariance
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;                         # level-1 (focal) model
  missingness:
  m ~ intercept group alpha beta | intercept;            # missingness model
  { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                              # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                             # random number seed
BURN: 25000;                                             # warm-up iterations
ITER: 25000;                                             # analysis iterations

rblimp

model2_gi <- rblimp(
  data = growth_intermittent,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (missing)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta',
  fixed = 'group time',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    alpha ~~ beta;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;
    missingness:
    m ~ intercept group alpha beta | intercept;
    { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 25000,
  iter = 25000)

output(model2_gi)

Model 3: Random Effects and Their Squares Predicting Missingness

Squared random effects allow both tails of the distribution to predict missingness.

Important features of the specification:

  • alpha^2 and beta^2 are the squared latent variables.

Blimp script

DATA: growth-intermittent.csv;                                # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                                  # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                              # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                                 # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (missing);                                     # missingness indicator (intermittent)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta;                                    # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                            # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                            # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                             # random slope equation
  alpha ~~ beta;                                              # random effect covariance
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;                              # level-1 (focal) model
  missingness:
  m ~ intercept group alpha alpha^2 beta beta^2 | intercept;  # missingness model
  { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;       # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                                   # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                                  # random number seed
BURN: 25000;                                                  # warm-up iterations
ITER: 25000;                                                  # analysis iterations

rblimp

model3_gi <- rblimp(
  data = growth_intermittent,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (missing)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta',
  fixed = 'group time',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    alpha ~~ beta;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;
    missingness:
    m ~ intercept group alpha alpha^2 beta beta^2 | intercept;
    { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 25000,
  iter = 25000)

output(model3_gi)

Model 4: Random Effect Residuals Predicting Missingness

The residualized version uses the level-2 residuals in place of the raw random effects.

Important features of the specification:

  • The residual definition variables are the same as in the dropout example; no switch is needed.

Blimp script

DATA: growth-intermittent.csv;                           # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                             # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                         # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                            # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (missing);                                # missingness indicator (intermittent)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta;                               # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                       # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                       # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                        # random slope equation
  alpha ~~ beta;                                         # random effect covariance
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;                         # level-1 (focal) model
  missingness:
  alpha_res = alpha - (g0a + g1a*group);                 # definition variable: intercept residual
  beta_res = beta - (g0b + g1b*group);                   # definition variable: slope residual
  m ~ intercept group alpha_res beta_res | intercept;    # missingness model
  { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                              # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                             # random number seed
BURN: 25000;                                             # warm-up iterations
ITER: 25000;                                             # analysis iterations

rblimp

model4_gi <- rblimp(
  data = growth_intermittent,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (missing)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta',
  fixed = 'group time',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    alpha ~~ beta;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;
    missingness:
    alpha_res = alpha - (g0a + g1a*group);
    beta_res = beta - (g0b + g1b*group);
    m ~ intercept group alpha_res beta_res | intercept;
    { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 25000,
  iter = 25000)

output(model4_gi)

Intensive Data With Dropout

In a stationary intensive design it is less obvious which random effects belong in the missingness model. The random intercept is the stable component of a person’s outcome (their average level) and is the natural first choice. Whether to include the random slope for a time-varying covariate is a substantive decision. The paper’s examples instead use the log-variance random effect \(\omega_i\), on the grounds that the magnitude of a person’s intraindividual variability is itself a plausible determinant of nonresponse: two people with the same average level can differ in how much they fluctuate, and the one with larger swings may find the protocol harder to sustain.

Dropout begins after occasion 7, so D switches at t = 7, and the occasion dummy codes are also multiplied by D as in the time-trend models.

\[M^*_{ti} = \lambda_0 + \sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\left[\lambda_{t0}(O_{ti})(D_{ti}) + \lambda_{t1}(O_{ti})(\mathit{GROUP}_i)(D_{ti})\right] + \lambda_1(\alpha_i)(D_{ti}) + \lambda_2(\omega_i)(D_{ti}) + z_{ti}\]

Model 2: Random Effects Predicting Attrition

The random intercept and the log-variance random effect, activated after occasion 7.

Important features of the specification:

  • d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1); switches at occasion 7.
  • alpha*d omega*d are the random intercept and log-variance, activated by d.
  • Both the random-effect terms and the dummy codes in the loop are multiplied by d.

Blimp script

DATA: intensive-dropout.csv;                                  # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                                  # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                              # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                                 # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (monotone);                                    # dropout indicator (monotone)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta omega;                              # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                            # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
CENTER: groupmean = x;                                        # latent group-mean centering of the level-1 covariate
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                            # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                             # random slope equation
  omega ~ intercept@g0o;                                      # log-variance equation
  alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;                       # random effect covariances
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;                                 # level-1 (focal) model
  var(y) ~ intercept@omega;                                   # within-person log-variance model
  missingness:
  d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1);                                 # definition variable: switch dummy code
  m ~ intercept@-3 alpha*d omega*d | intercept@0;             # missingness model
  { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t])*d (time == [t])*group*d;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                                   # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = g1a;
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                                  # random number seed
BURN: 75000;                                                  # warm-up iterations
ITER: 75000;                                                  # analysis iterations

rblimp

model2_id <- rblimp(
  data = intensive_dropout,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (monotone)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta omega',
  fixed = 'group time',
  center = 'groupmean = x',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    omega ~ intercept@g0o;
    alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;
    var(y) ~ intercept@omega;
    missingness:
    d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1);
    m ~ intercept@-3 alpha*d omega*d | intercept@0;
    { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t])*d (time == [t])*group*d;',
  parameters = '
    diff = g1a;
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 75000,
  iter = 75000)

output(model2_id)

Model 3: Random Effects and Their Squares Predicting Attrition

Squared terms for both random effects.

Important features of the specification:

  • This model reached the 200,000-iteration cap and is flagged as inadmissible in Table 4.

Blimp script

DATA: intensive-dropout.csv;                                           # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                                           # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                                       # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                                          # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (monotone);                                             # dropout indicator (monotone)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta omega;                                       # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                                     # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
CENTER: groupmean = x;                                                 # latent group-mean centering of the level-1 covariate
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                                     # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                                      # random slope equation
  omega ~ intercept@g0o;                                               # log-variance equation
  alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;                                # random effect covariances
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;                                          # level-1 (focal) model
  var(y) ~ intercept@omega;                                            # within-person log-variance model
  missingness:
  d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1);                                          # definition variable: switch dummy code
  m ~ intercept@-3 alpha*d omega*d alpha^2*d omega^2*d | intercept@0;  # missingness model
  { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t])*d (time == [t])*group*d;           # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                                            # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = g1a;
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                                           # random number seed
BURN: 200000;                                                          # warm-up iterations
ITER: 200000;                                                          # analysis iterations

rblimp

model3_id <- rblimp(
  data = intensive_dropout,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (monotone)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta omega',
  fixed = 'group time',
  center = 'groupmean = x',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    omega ~ intercept@g0o;
    alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;
    var(y) ~ intercept@omega;
    missingness:
    d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1);
    m ~ intercept@-3 alpha*d omega*d alpha^2*d omega^2*d | intercept@0;
    { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t])*d (time == [t])*group*d;',
  parameters = '
    diff = g1a;
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 200000,
  iter = 200000)

output(model3_id)

ALGORITHMIC OPTIONS SPECIFIED:

  Imputation method:                 Fully Bayesian model-based
  MCMC algorithm:                    Full conditional Metropolis sampler with
                                       Auto-Derived Conditional Distributions
  Default Priors:
    Multilevel covariance matrices:  Zero matrix, df = -(p + 1) (PRIOR2)
    Outcome covariance matrices:     Zero matrix, df = -(p + 1) (PRIOR2)
    Predictor model variances:       Unit sum of squares, df = 2 (XPRIOR1)
  Chain Starting Values:             Random starting values

Model 4: Random Effect Residuals Predicting Attrition

The random intercept residual replaces the raw random intercept. Because omega has no level-2 predictors, it is already a residual and enters as is.

Important features of the specification:

  • alpha_res = alpha - (g0a + g1a*group); uses the labeled level-2 coefficients.

Blimp script

DATA: intensive-dropout.csv;                                  # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                                  # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                              # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                                 # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (monotone);                                    # dropout indicator (monotone)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta omega;                              # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                            # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
CENTER: groupmean = x;                                        # latent group-mean centering of the level-1 covariate
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                            # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                             # random slope equation
  omega ~ intercept@g0o;                                      # log-variance equation
  alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;                       # random effect covariances
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;                                 # level-1 (focal) model
  var(y) ~ intercept@omega;                                   # within-person log-variance model
  missingness:
  d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1);                                 # definition variable: switch dummy code
  alpha_res = alpha - (g0a + g1a*group);                      # definition variable: intercept residual
  m ~ intercept@-3 d*alpha_res d*omega | intercept@0;         # missingness model
  { t in 1:19 } : m ~ d*(time == [t]) d*(time == [t])*group;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                                   # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = g1a;
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                                  # random number seed
BURN: 25000;                                                  # warm-up iterations
ITER: 25000;                                                  # analysis iterations

rblimp

model4_id <- rblimp(
  data = intensive_dropout,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (monotone)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta omega',
  fixed = 'group time',
  center = 'groupmean = x',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    omega ~ intercept@g0o;
    alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;
    var(y) ~ intercept@omega;
    missingness:
    d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1);
    alpha_res = alpha - (g0a + g1a*group);
    m ~ intercept@-3 d*alpha_res d*omega | intercept@0;
    { t in 1:19 } : m ~ d*(time == [t]) d*(time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = g1a;
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 25000,
  iter = 25000)

output(model4_id)

Model 5: Random Effects and X Latent Means Predicting Attrition

When both X and Y are missing at the same occasions, M indicates joint nonresponse. If the unseen X scores plausibly relate to attrition, the level-2 latent mean of X can be added as a shared parameter, so that nonresponse depends on the unobserved values of both variables. Blimp constructs a background model for X to estimate its person means and impute its missing values.

\[M^*_{ti} = \lambda_0 + \sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\left[\lambda_{t0}(O_{ti})(D_{ti}) + \lambda_{t1}(O_{ti})(\mathit{GROUP}_i)(D_{ti})\right] + \lambda_1(\alpha_i)(D_{ti}) + \lambda_2(\omega_i)(D_{ti}) + \lambda_3(\mu_{Xi})(D_{ti}) + z_{ti}\]

Important features of the specification:

  • x.mean is the latent person mean of x, the same quantity used by CENTER: groupmean = x.
  • This model reached the 200,000-iteration cap and is flagged as inadmissible in Table 4.

Blimp script

DATA: intensive-dropout.csv;                                  # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                                  # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                              # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                                 # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (monotone);                                    # dropout indicator (monotone)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta omega;                              # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                            # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
CENTER: groupmean = x;                                        # latent group-mean centering of the level-1 covariate
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                            # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                             # random slope equation
  omega ~ intercept@g0o;                                      # log-variance equation
  alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;                       # random effect covariances
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;                                 # level-1 (focal) model
  var(y) ~ intercept@omega;                                   # within-person log-variance model
  missingness:
  d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1);                                 # definition variable: switch dummy code
  m ~ intercept@-3 d*alpha d*omega d*x.mean | intercept@0;    # missingness model
  { t in 1:19 } : m ~ d*(time == [t]) d*(time == [t])*group;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                                   # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = g1a;
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                                  # random number seed
BURN: 200000;                                                 # warm-up iterations
ITER: 200000;                                                 # analysis iterations

rblimp

model5_id <- rblimp(
  data = intensive_dropout,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (monotone)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta omega',
  fixed = 'group time',
  center = 'groupmean = x',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    omega ~ intercept@g0o;
    alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;
    var(y) ~ intercept@omega;
    missingness:
    d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1);
    m ~ intercept@-3 d*alpha d*omega d*x.mean | intercept@0;
    { t in 1:19 } : m ~ d*(time == [t]) d*(time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = g1a;
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 200000,
  iter = 200000)

output(model5_id)

Intensive Data With Intermittent Missingness

The intermittent versions parallel the growth models: no switch, an estimable intercept, a group main effect, and a random intercept in the missingness model. The log-variance random effect replaces the random slope as a predictor.

Model 2: Random Effects Predicting Missingness

Random intercept and log-variance predicting missingness.

Blimp script

DATA: intensive-intermittent.csv;                         # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                              # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                          # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                             # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (missing);                                 # missingness indicator (intermittent)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta omega;                          # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                        # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
CENTER: groupmean = x;                                    # latent group-mean centering of the level-1 covariate
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                        # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                         # random slope equation
  omega ~ intercept@g0o;                                  # log-variance equation
  alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;                   # random effect covariances
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;                             # level-1 (focal) model
  var(y) ~ intercept@omega;                               # within-person log-variance model
  missingness:
  m ~ intercept group alpha omega | intercept;            # missingness model
  { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                               # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = g1a;
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                              # random number seed
BURN: 25000;                                              # warm-up iterations
ITER: 25000;                                              # analysis iterations

rblimp

model2_ii <- rblimp(
  data = intensive_intermittent,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (missing)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta omega',
  fixed = 'group time',
  center = 'groupmean = x',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    omega ~ intercept@g0o;
    alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;
    var(y) ~ intercept@omega;
    missingness:
    m ~ intercept group alpha omega | intercept;
    { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = g1a;
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 25000,
  iter = 25000)

output(model2_ii)

Model 3: Random Effects and Their Squares Predicting Missingness

Squared random effects.

Blimp script

DATA: intensive-intermittent.csv;                               # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                                    # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                                # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                                   # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (missing);                                       # missingness indicator (intermittent)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta omega;                                # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                              # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
CENTER: groupmean = x;                                          # latent group-mean centering of the level-1 covariate
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                              # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                               # random slope equation
  omega ~ intercept@g0o;                                        # log-variance equation
  alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;                         # random effect covariances
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;                                   # level-1 (focal) model
  var(y) ~ intercept@omega;                                     # within-person log-variance model
  missingness:
  m ~ intercept group alpha alpha^2 omega omega^2 | intercept;  # missingness model
  { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;        # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                                     # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = g1a;
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                                    # random number seed
BURN: 25000;                                                    # warm-up iterations
ITER: 25000;                                                    # analysis iterations

rblimp

model3_ii <- rblimp(
  data = intensive_intermittent,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (missing)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta omega',
  fixed = 'group time',
  center = 'groupmean = x',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    omega ~ intercept@g0o;
    alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;
    var(y) ~ intercept@omega;
    missingness:
    m ~ intercept group alpha alpha^2 omega omega^2 | intercept;
    { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = g1a;
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 25000,
  iter = 25000)

output(model3_ii)

Model 4: Random Effect Residuals Predicting Missingness

Residualized random intercept with the log-variance random effect.

Blimp script

DATA: intensive-intermittent.csv;                         # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                              # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                          # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                             # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (missing);                                 # missingness indicator (intermittent)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta omega;                          # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                        # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
CENTER: groupmean = x;                                    # latent group-mean centering of the level-1 covariate
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                        # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                         # random slope equation
  omega ~ intercept@g0o;                                  # log-variance equation
  alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;                   # random effect covariances
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;                             # level-1 (focal) model
  var(y) ~ intercept@omega;                               # within-person log-variance model
  missingness:
  alpha_res = alpha - (g0a + g1a*group);                  # definition variable: intercept residual
  m ~ intercept group alpha_res omega | intercept;        # missingness model
  { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                               # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = g1a;
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                              # random number seed
BURN: 25000;                                              # warm-up iterations
ITER: 25000;                                              # analysis iterations

rblimp

model4_ii <- rblimp(
  data = intensive_intermittent,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (missing)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta omega',
  fixed = 'group time',
  center = 'groupmean = x',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    omega ~ intercept@g0o;
    alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;
    var(y) ~ intercept@omega;
    missingness:
    alpha_res = alpha - (g0a + g1a*group);
    m ~ intercept group alpha_res omega | intercept;
    { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = g1a;
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 25000,
  iter = 25000)

output(model4_ii)

Model 5: Random Effects and X Latent Means Predicting Missingness

Adds the latent person mean of X.

Blimp script

DATA: intensive-intermittent.csv;                         # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                              # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                          # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                             # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (missing);                                 # missingness indicator (intermittent)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta omega;                          # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                        # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
CENTER: groupmean = x;                                    # latent group-mean centering of the level-1 covariate
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                        # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                         # random slope equation
  omega ~ intercept@g0o;                                  # log-variance equation
  alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;                   # random effect covariances
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;                             # level-1 (focal) model
  var(y) ~ intercept@omega;                               # within-person log-variance model
  missingness:
  m ~ intercept group alpha omega x.mean | intercept;     # missingness model
  { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                               # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = g1a;
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                              # random number seed
BURN: 25000;                                              # warm-up iterations
ITER: 25000;                                              # analysis iterations

rblimp

model5_ii <- rblimp(
  data = intensive_intermittent,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (missing)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta omega',
  fixed = 'group time',
  center = 'groupmean = x',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    omega ~ intercept@g0o;
    alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;
    var(y) ~ intercept@omega;
    missingness:
    m ~ intercept group alpha omega x.mean | intercept;
    { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = g1a;
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 25000,
  iter = 25000)

output(model5_ii)

Selection Models

In the Diggle–Kenward (1994) selection model, occasion-specific realizations of the outcome, rather than stable levels or trends, drive nonresponse. The multilevel version requires a lagged outcome \(Y_{t-1}\) that shifts each person’s scores down by one row; Blimp’s DSEM facilities create and impute lagged variables when a variable name carries the .lag suffix. Lagging requires each person to have a row for every occasion, and Blimp inserts missing rows to make the data time-balanced if they are not.

Growth Data With Dropout

The structure parallels the shared parameter model: the fixed intercept of –3 replaces the omitted baseline indicator, and products with D confine the outcome and its lag to post-baseline occasions.

\[M^*_{ti} = \lambda_0 + \sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\left[\lambda_{t0}(O_{ti}) + \lambda_{t1}(O_{ti})(\mathit{GROUP}_i)\right] + \lambda_1(Y_{ti})(D_{ti}) + \lambda_2(Y_{t-1,i})(D_{ti}) + z_{ti}\]

The \(\lambda_1\) term induces the MNAR mechanism: the unobserved value of Y influences attrition after conditioning on the observed data.

Model 5: Outcome and its Lag Predicting Attrition

The outcome and its lag, switched on after baseline.

Important features of the specification:

  • y*d y.lag*d – y.lag is the previous occasion’s outcome, created by Blimp from timeid.
  • At baseline y.lag does not exist; d = 0 there, so the term contributes nothing.

Blimp script

DATA: growth-dropout.csv;                                # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                             # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                         # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                            # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (monotone);                               # dropout indicator (monotone)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta;                               # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                       # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                       # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                        # random slope equation
  alpha ~~ beta;                                         # random effect covariance
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;                         # level-1 (focal) model
  missingness:
  d = ifelse(time < 1, 0, 1);                            # definition variable: switch dummy code
  m ~ intercept@-3 y*d y.lag*d | intercept@0;            # missingness model
  { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                              # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                             # random number seed
BURN: 25000;                                             # warm-up iterations
ITER: 25000;                                             # analysis iterations

rblimp

model5_gd <- rblimp(
  data = growth_dropout,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
    dropout = 'm = y (monotone)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta',
  fixed = 'group time',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    alpha ~~ beta;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;
    missingness:
    d = ifelse(time < 1, 0, 1);
    m ~ intercept@-3 y*d y.lag*d | intercept@0;
    { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 25000,
  iter = 25000)

output(model5_gd)

Model 6: Outcome, its Lag, and its Square Predicting Attrition

A linear term lets only one tail of the outcome distribution predict higher attrition. Adding \(Y^2\) allows both sudden increases and sudden decreases to raise the probability of dropout.

Important features of the specification:

  • y^2*d is the squared outcome, activated after baseline.
  • This model is flagged as inadmissible in Table 2 because of its large pseudo-\(R^2\).

Blimp script

DATA: growth-dropout.csv;                                # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                             # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                         # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                            # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (monotone);                               # dropout indicator (monotone)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta;                               # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                       # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                       # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                        # random slope equation
  alpha ~~ beta;                                         # random effect covariance
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;                         # level-1 (focal) model
  missingness:
  d = ifelse(time < 1, 0, 1);                            # definition variable: switch dummy code
  m ~ intercept@-3 y*d y^2*d y.lag*d | intercept@0;      # missingness model
  { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                              # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                             # random number seed
BURN: 50000;                                             # warm-up iterations
ITER: 50000;                                             # analysis iterations

rblimp

model6_gd <- rblimp(
  data = growth_dropout,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (monotone)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta',
  fixed = 'group time',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    alpha ~~ beta;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;
    missingness:
    d = ifelse(time < 1, 0, 1);
    m ~ intercept@-3 y*d y^2*d y.lag*d | intercept@0;
    { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 50000,
  iter = 50000)

output(model6_gd)

Model 7: Detrended Outcome and its Lag Predicting Attrition

The raw Y values are composites of a person’s trajectory and occasion-specific deviations, so \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\) in Model 5 are blended within- and between-person slopes. Detrending subtracts each person’s model-implied trajectory value, isolating episodic shifts from expected behavior. The detrending happens inside each MCMC iteration using the current random effects (a residual DSEM). Neither version is more correct; the raw-score model emphasizes absolute standing, the detrended model targets deviations from expected behavior.

\[Y^{w}_{ti} = Y_{ti} - \left(\alpha_i + \beta_i(\mathit{TIME}_{ti})\right) \qquad Y^{w}_{t-1,i} = Y_{t-1,i} - \left(\alpha_i + \beta_i(\mathit{TIME}_{ti} - 1)\right)\]

Important features of the specification:

  • yw = y - (alpha + beta*time); and lagyw = y.lag - (alpha + beta*(time - 1)); are definition variables for the detrended outcome and its lag.
  • This model required 200,000 iterations and is flagged as inadmissible in Table 2.

Blimp script

DATA: growth-dropout.csv;                                # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                             # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                         # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                            # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (monotone);                               # dropout indicator (monotone)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta;                               # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                       # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                       # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                        # random slope equation
  alpha ~~ beta;                                         # random effect covariance
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;                         # level-1 (focal) model
  missingness:
  d = ifelse(time < 1, 0, 1);                            # definition variable: switch dummy code
  yw = y - (alpha + beta*time);                          # definition variable: detrended outcome
  lagyw = y.lag - (alpha + beta*(time - 1));             # definition variable: detrended lag
  m ~ intercept@-3 yw*d lagyw*d | intercept@0;           # missingness model
  { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                              # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                             # random number seed
BURN: 200000;                                            # warm-up iterations
ITER: 200000;                                            # analysis iterations

rblimp

model7_gd <- rblimp(
  data = growth_dropout,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (monotone)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta',
  fixed = 'group time',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    alpha ~~ beta;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;
    missingness:
    d = ifelse(time < 1, 0, 1);
    yw = y - (alpha + beta*time);
    lagyw = y.lag - (alpha + beta*(time - 1));
    m ~ intercept@-3 yw*d lagyw*d | intercept@0;
    { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 200000,
  iter = 200000)

Growth Data With Intermittent Missingness

With missingness at every occasion the switch is unnecessary, the intercept and group effect are estimable, and a random intercept is added.

\[M^*_{ti} = \lambda_0 + \lambda_1(\mathit{GROUP}_i) + \sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\left[\lambda_{t0}(O_{ti}) + \lambda_{t1}(O_{ti})(\mathit{GROUP}_i)\right] + \lambda_2(Y_{ti}) + \lambda_3(Y_{t-1,i}) + u_i + z_{ti}\]

This model differs subtly from the SEM in Figure 2D of the paper, which has no cross-lagged effect for the baseline indicator. Here Blimp imputes the missing lagged value in each person’s first row, which requires a prior distribution for that value; Blimp’s default prior was chosen for its performance in simulations. An alternative that activates the lagged predictor only after baseline is shown after Model 5.

Model 5: Outcome and its Lag Predicting Missingness

The outcome and its lag with no switch.

Blimp script

DATA: growth-intermittent.csv;                           # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                             # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                         # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                            # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (missing);                                # missingness indicator (intermittent)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta;                               # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                       # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                       # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                        # random slope equation
  alpha ~~ beta;                                         # random effect covariance
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;                         # level-1 (focal) model
  missingness:
  m ~ intercept group y y.lag | intercept;               # missingness model
  { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                              # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                             # random number seed
BURN: 25000;                                             # warm-up iterations
ITER: 25000;                                             # analysis iterations

rblimp

model5_gi <- rblimp(
  data = growth_intermittent,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (missing)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta',
  fixed = 'group time',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    alpha ~~ beta;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;
    missingness:
    m ~ intercept group y y.lag | intercept;
    { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 25000,
  iter = 25000)

output(model5_gi)

Alternate Specification: Lag Activated After Baseline

The specification below replaces the imputed baseline lag with zero, which is analogous to the wide-format SEM that omits the cross-lagged effect at the first occasion. In the illustrative data the two approaches give the same focal-model estimates.

Important features of the specification:

  • y_lag = ifelse(time == 0, 0, y.lag); is a definition variable that returns 0 at baseline and the lagged outcome elsewhere, so the baseline lag never enters the model.

Blimp script

DATA: growth-intermittent.csv;                           # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                             # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                         # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                            # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (missing);                                # missingness indicator (intermittent)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta;                               # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                       # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                       # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                        # random slope equation
  alpha ~~ beta;                                         # random effect covariance
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;                         # level-1 (focal) model
  missingness:
  y_lag = ifelse(time == 0, 0, y.lag);                   # definition variable: zero at baseline
  m ~ intercept group y y_lag | intercept;               # missingness model
  { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                              # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                             # random number seed
BURN: 25000;                                             # warm-up iterations
ITER: 25000;                                             # analysis iterations

rblimp

model5_alt_gi <- rblimp(
  data = growth_intermittent,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (missing)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta',
  fixed = 'group time',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    alpha ~~ beta;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;
    missingness:
    y_lag = ifelse(time == 0, 0, y.lag);
    m ~ intercept group y y_lag | intercept;
    { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 25000,
  iter = 25000)

output(model5_alt_gi)

Model 7: Detrended Outcome and its Lag Predicting Missingness

Detrended outcome and lag.

Important features of the specification:

  • Flagged as inadmissible in Table 3 (200,000 iterations, large pseudo-\(R^2\)).

Blimp script

DATA: growth-intermittent.csv;                           # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                             # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                         # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                            # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (missing);                                # missingness indicator (intermittent)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta;                               # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                       # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                       # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                        # random slope equation
  alpha ~~ beta;                                         # random effect covariance
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;                         # level-1 (focal) model
  missingness:
  yw = y - (alpha + beta*time);                          # definition variable: detrended outcome
  lagyw = y.lag - (alpha + beta*(time - 1));             # definition variable: detrended lag
  m ~ intercept group yw lagyw | intercept;              # missingness model
  { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                              # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                             # random number seed
BURN: 200000;                                            # warm-up iterations
ITER: 200000;                                            # analysis iterations

rblimp

model7_gi <- rblimp(
  data = growth_intermittent,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (missing)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta',
  fixed = 'group time',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    alpha ~~ beta;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha time@beta;
    missingness:
    yw = y - (alpha + beta*time);
    lagyw = y.lag - (alpha + beta*(time - 1));
    m ~ intercept group yw lagyw | intercept;
    { t in 1:4 } : m ~ (time == [t]) (time == [t])*group;',
  parameters = '
    diff = (((g0a+g1a)  + 4*(g0b+g1b)) - (g0a + 4*g0b));
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(y.totalvar + alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 200000,
  iter = 200000)

output(model7_gi)

Intensive Data With Dropout

Including the outcome and its lag is also natural for intensive data, where a person’s current or previous state can influence nonresponse. The switch now activates at occasion 7.

\[M^*_{ti} = \lambda_0 + \sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\left[\lambda_{t0}(O_{ti})(D_{ti}) + \lambda_{t1}(O_{ti})(\mathit{GROUP}_i)(D_{ti})\right] + \lambda_1(Y_{ti})(D_{ti}) + \lambda_2(Y_{t-1,i})(D_{ti}) + z_{ti}\]

Model 6: Outcome and its Lag Predicting Attrition

Outcome and lag, switched on at occasion 7.

Blimp script

DATA: intensive-dropout.csv;                                  # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                                  # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                              # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                                 # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (monotone);                                    # dropout indicator (monotone)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta omega;                              # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                            # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
CENTER: groupmean = x;                                        # latent group-mean centering of the level-1 covariate
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                            # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                             # random slope equation
  omega ~ intercept@g0o;                                      # log-variance equation
  alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;                       # random effect covariances
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;                                 # level-1 (focal) model
  var(y) ~ intercept@omega;                                   # within-person log-variance model
  missingness:
  d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1);                                 # definition variable: switch dummy code
  m ~ intercept@-3 y*d y.lag*d | intercept@0;                 # missingness model
  { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t])*d (time == [t])*group*d;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                                   # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = g1a;
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                                  # random number seed
BURN: 25000;                                                  # warm-up iterations
ITER: 25000;                                                  # analysis iterations

rblimp

model6_id <- rblimp(
  data = intensive_dropout,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (monotone)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta omega',
  fixed = 'group time',
  center = 'groupmean = x',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    omega ~ intercept@g0o;
    alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;
    var(y) ~ intercept@omega;
    missingness:
    d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1);
    m ~ intercept@-3 y*d y.lag*d | intercept@0;
    { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t])*d (time == [t])*group*d;',
  parameters = '
    diff = g1a;
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 25000,
  iter = 25000)

output(model6_id)

Model 7: Outcome, its Lag, and its Square Predicting Attrition

Adds the squared outcome.

Important features of the specification:

  • Flagged as inadmissible in Table 4 (200,000 iterations, pseudo-\(R^2\) = .96).

Blimp script

DATA: intensive-dropout.csv;                                  # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                                  # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                              # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                                 # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (monotone);                                    # dropout indicator (monotone)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta omega;                              # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                            # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
CENTER: groupmean = x;                                        # latent group-mean centering of the level-1 covariate
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                            # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                             # random slope equation
  omega ~ intercept@g0o;                                      # log-variance equation
  alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;                       # random effect covariances
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;                                 # level-1 (focal) model
  var(y) ~ intercept@omega;                                   # within-person log-variance model
  missingness:
  d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1);                                 # definition variable: switch dummy code
  m ~ intercept@-3 y*d y^2*d y.lag*d | intercept@0;           # missingness model
  { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t])*d (time == [t])*group*d;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                                   # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = g1a;
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                                  # random number seed
BURN: 200000;                                                 # warm-up iterations
ITER: 200000;                                                 # analysis iterations

rblimp

model7_id <- rblimp(
  data = intensive_dropout,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (monotone)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta omega',
  fixed = 'group time',
  center = 'groupmean = x',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    omega ~ intercept@g0o;
    alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;
    var(y) ~ intercept@omega;
    missingness:
    d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1);
    m ~ intercept@-3 y*d y^2*d y.lag*d | intercept@0;
    { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t])*d (time == [t])*group*d;',
  parameters = '
    diff = g1a;
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 200000,
  iter = 200000)

output(model7_id)

Model 8: Centered Outcome and its Lag Predicting Attrition

In a stationary process the raw Y is the sum of a person’s latent mean and an occasion-specific deviation, so the raw-score slopes are again blended. McNeish (2025) subtracts the latent person mean (the random intercept) from the raw outcomes; the centering is carried out within each MCMC iteration using the current random intercept.

\[M^*_{ti} = \lambda_0 + \sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\left[\lambda_{t0}(O_{ti})(D_{ti}) + \lambda_{t1}(O_{ti})(\mathit{GROUP}_i)(D_{ti})\right] + \lambda_1(Y_{ti} - \alpha_i)(D_{ti}) + \lambda_2(Y_{t-1,i} - \alpha_i)(D_{ti}) + z_{ti}\]

Important features of the specification:

  • (y - alpha)*d and (y.lag - alpha)*d center the outcome and its lag at the random intercept inline, without definition variables.

Blimp script

DATA: intensive-dropout.csv;                                       # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                                       # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                                   # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                                      # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (monotone);                                         # dropout indicator (monotone)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta omega;                                   # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                                 # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
CENTER: groupmean = x;                                             # latent group-mean centering of the level-1 covariate
MODEL:
  level2:
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                                 # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                                  # random slope equation
  omega ~ intercept@g0o;                                           # log-variance equation
  alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;                            # random effect covariances
  level1:
  y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;                                      # level-1 (focal) model
  var(y) ~ intercept@omega;                                        # within-person log-variance model
  missingness:
  d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1);                                      # definition variable: switch dummy code
  m ~ intercept@-3 (y - alpha)*d (y.lag - alpha)*d | intercept@0;  # missingness model
  { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t])*d (time == [t])*group*d;       # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                                        # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = g1a;
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                                       # random number seed
BURN: 75000;                                                       # warm-up iterations
ITER: 75000;                                                       # analysis iterations

rblimp

model8_id <- rblimp(
  data = intensive_dropout,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (monotone)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta omega',
  fixed = 'group time',
  center = 'groupmean = x',
  model = '
    level2:
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    omega ~ intercept@g0o;
    alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;
    level1:
    y ~ intercept@alpha x@beta;
    var(y) ~ intercept@omega;
    missingness:
    d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1);
    m ~ intercept@-3 (y - alpha)*d (y.lag - alpha)*d | intercept@0;
    { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t])*d (time == [t])*group*d;',
  parameters = '
    diff = g1a;
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 75000,
  iter = 75000)

output(model8_id)

Model 9: Outcome, its Lag, and X Predicting Attrition

When X and Y are jointly missing, the covariate and its lag can be added to the dropout model so that nonresponse depends on the unseen values of both variables.

Important features of the specification:

  • x*d x.lag*d add the covariate and its lag; Blimp imputes missing x from its background model.

Blimp script

DATA: intensive-dropout.csv;                                  # raw data file
MISSING: NA;                                                  # missing value code
CLUSTERID: l2id;                                              # level-2 identifier
TIMEID: time;                                                 # occasion index for lags and dropout coding
DROPOUT: m = y (monotone);                                    # dropout indicator (monotone)
LATENT: l2id = alpha beta omega xmeans;                       # level-2 latent variables (random effects)
FIXED: group time;                                            # complete predictors (speeds estimation)
MODEL:
  level2:
  xmeans ~ intercept;
  alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;                            # random intercept equation
  beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;                             # random slope equation
  omega ~ intercept@g0o;                                      # log-variance equation
  alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;                       # random effect covariances
  level1:
  x ~ intercept@xmeans;
  y ~ intercept@alpha (x - xmeans)@beta;                      # level-1 (focal) model
  var(y) ~ intercept@omega;                                   # within-person log-variance model
  missingness:
  d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1);                                 # definition variable: switch dummy code
  m ~ intercept@-3 y*d y.lag*d x*d x.lag*d | intercept@0;     # missingness model
  { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t])*d (time == [t])*group*d;  # loop adds occasion dummy codes
PARAMETERS:                                                   # derived quantities (effect sizes)
  diff = g1a;
  d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);
SEED: 90291;                                                  # random number seed
BURN: 25000;                                                  # warm-up iterations
ITER: 25000;                                                  # analysis iterations

rblimp

model9_id <- rblimp(
  data = intensive_dropout,
  clusterid = 'l2id',
  timeid = 'time',
  dropout = 'm = y (monotone)',
  latent = 'l2id = alpha beta omega xmeans',
  fixed = 'group time',
  model = '
    level2:
    xmeans ~ intercept;
    alpha ~ intercept@g0a group@g1a;
    beta ~ intercept@g0b group@g1b;
    omega ~ intercept@g0o;
    alpha beta omega ~~ alpha beta omega;
    level1:
    x ~ intercept@xmeans;
    y ~ intercept@alpha (x - xmeans)@beta;
    var(y) ~ intercept@omega;
    missingness:
    d = ifelse(time < 7, 0, 1);
    m ~ intercept@-3 y*d y.lag*d x*d x.lag*d | intercept@0;
    { t in 1:19 } : m ~ (time == [t])*d (time == [t])*group*d;',
  parameters = '
    diff = g1a;
    d_diff = diff / sqrt(alpha.totalvar);',
  seed = 90291,
  burn = 25000,
  iter = 25000)

output(model9_id)
